name: Gabriel Han
life: “I still remember a parasol jumping a hotel fence during tea.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the corner by Juniper Tailor, where Gabriel looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I promised never to leave things on the beach. I stayed until both owners went home dry.
appearance: Gabriel has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for brown hair pinned away from the temples. Back on the street, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. In conversation Gabriel rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Gabriel takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To wait until nobody has to go home in the rain.
family: Olivia Teo is Gabriel’s half-sibling. Gabriel offers the first invitation. Olivia gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Olivia says, “I sign my wife's name for deliveries. Tonight I want to learn to write mine on a wage dispute.”
connections: Eileen Reed. The fabric worker helps distinguish two umbrellas before anyone walks home in rain.

reactions.situation: A hotel worker asks to throw the patched umbrella away
reactions.response: Gabriel puts the patched umbrella aside until the owner can explain the repair.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Gabriel stays beside the bystander in a public place and reports only what happened in sight and earshot.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Gabriel asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
